text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- Croatia will extend concessions to foreign and domestic firms for eight zones with tax and customs priviledges, which are to be established by spring. The competition is open for another 50 days and firms from Austria, Germany and Netherlands already sent their offers.
- With Italian lira on a rise against Croatian kuna, hopes are high their tourist would be more attracted to spend their summer vacations on Croatian coast, says Lidija Martinovic in an analysis.
- Food concern Podravka is now the most interesting stock on the market. Last week its price went up 14 percent on volume of 19 million kuna and the trend is likely to continue.
- Real estate bourse in Zagreb reports of growing demand for high quality bigger flats and of better renting prices as market stabilises after the war.
- Unimployed participants of 1991-95 war against the rebel Serbs will get a 900 kuna monthly aid according to new law.
- Prices of audio and video appliances can vary by up to 30 percent in different shops in the Croatian capital.
- Long-term loans for purchase of flats should help to solve problems of the young and a large majority of employees, according to new law which should reach the parliament in February.
- Bosnian Moslems no longer behave as partners but are trying to dominate the Bosnian-Croat federation, says deputy chairman of the federal ministerial board Neven Tomic, a Croat.
- Famed hotel Imperial in the historical town of Dubrovnik, built a 100 years ago needs substantial investment, but new owner is still undecided. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
